react.wrong: Oops! A ball on the floor!
react.late: Too slow! My pins keep spinning.

generic.tagline: A section guardian: it checks that you remembered well.
generic.defeat: Well played, what comes next is yours.
generic.win: Not this time. Come back whenever you like.

jongleur.name: The Juggler
jongleur.tagline: He spins squares, moves and pieces… and waits for you to drop one.
jongleur.taunt: Three balls in the air, and you're still looking at the board?
jongleur.defeat: Nice catch! I'm putting my pins away… for this time.
jongleur.win: A ball on the floor! Shall we start over?

cyclope.name: The Cyclops
cyclope.tagline: A single eye, but a perfect memory.
cyclope.taunt: One look is enough for me. And you, how many do you need?
cyclope.defeat: You see as well as I do… with your eyes closed.
cyclope.win: My eye remembered everything. Yours, not yet.

gargouille.name: The Gargoyle
gargouille.tagline: It howls, grimaces and makes the board shake. Keep the thread.
gargouille.defeat: Grrr… even my screams weren't enough.

fantome.name: The Ghost
fantome.tagline: Pieces fade away as it passes. It's up to you to find them.
fantome.taunt: Can't see anything anymore? Neither can I… and yet.
fantome.defeat: You sense the pieces even when they disappear.
fantome.win: Boo… a piece flew out of your head.

cameleon.name: The Chameleon
cameleon.tagline: Its pieces change clothes on every move.
cameleon.taunt: That bishop looks like a knight? Look closer.

sith.name: The Blind Sith
sith.tagline: He plays whole games without ever seeing the board.
sith.defeat: The inner eye is within you.
sith.win: You were looking for the board. There is none.

sablier.name: The Hourglass
sablier.tagline: Time runs out, and it asks you to hold two positions at once.
sablier.taunt: Keep this one in mind… while I show you another.
sablier.defeat: Two positions, not a grain lost.

flash.name: The Flash
flash.tagline: Half a second. Not one more.
flash.win: Too slow… the position is already far away.

metronome.name: The Metronome
metronome.tagline: Tick, tock. It beats time and never stops: every correct line speeds up the tempo.
metronome.taunt: One beat late, and the rhythm is lost.
metronome.defeat: Out of tune… you kept the pace.
metronome.win: Tick, tock: you lost the tempo.

compteur.name: The Counter
compteur.tagline: He counts every move of a long variation and asks you where it ends.
compteur.taunt: How many moves can you hold before you lose count?
compteur.defeat: The count is right… for you.

avocat.name: The Devil's Advocate
avocat.tagline: You propose a move, he looks for the refutation. Find it before he does.
avocat.taunt: Your idea is tempting. Defend it.
avocat.defeat: Objection overruled: your idea held up.
avocat.win: Your idea does not stand up to scrutiny.

s1_1.title: Click the square
s1_1.desc: You're given “e4”, you click the square. One minute, at least 10 answers and 80% correct.

s1_2.title: Name the square
s1_2.desc: A square lights up on the board: give its name, file then rank. One minute, at least 10 answers and 80% correct.

s1_3.title: Square color
s1_3.desc: A square name, no board: light or dark? One minute, at least 20 answers and 80% correct.

s1_chest.title: Chest
s1_chest.desc: Pass the first three exercises to open it.

s1_5.title: Sequence of written moves
s1_5.desc: Play a sequence of written moves, taken from a puzzle or a repertoire.

s1_6.title: Write the solution
s1_6.desc: Write a puzzle's solution in notation.

s1_chest_2.title: Chest
s1_chest_2.desc: Pass the first six exercises to open it.

s1_7.title: Complete a line
s1_7.desc: A line from your repertoire plays out: write its last moves. You need a repertoire with at least 10 segments.

s1_8.title: Write down a famous game
s1_8.desc: Rebuild the notation of a famous game.

s1_9.title: Replay a famous game
s1_9.desc: Replay a famous game on the board from its notation.

s1_boss.title: The Juggler
s1_boss.desc: A fast sequence of the chapter's exercises: coordinates, notation and moves, with slight distractions.

s2_1_2.title: Two pawns

s2_1_3.title: Four pawns
s2_1_3.desc: Both kings, three white pawns, one black pawn.

s2_1_4.title: The first bishop
s2_1_4.desc: Both kings, a white bishop, three pawns.

s2_1_boss.title: Three positions
s2_1_boss.desc: Rebuild three positions in a row, without any visual clue.

s2_2_1.title: Seven pieces
s2_2_1.desc: Both kings, a bishop, four pawns: 11 seconds.

s2_2_2.title: Two bishops
s2_2_2.desc: Both kings, two bishops, four pawns: tell two identical pieces apart.

s2_2_3.title: The knight
s2_2_3.desc: Both kings, a knight, four pawns: unusual moves.

s2_2_4.title: The rook
s2_2_4.desc: Both kings, a rook, five pawns: the alignments.

s2_2_boss.title: Memory and question
s2_2_boss.desc: Memorize a position, then answer: “Where is the black king?”

s2_3_1.title: The queen
s2_3_1.desc: Both kings, a queen, five pawns: 14 seconds.

s2_3_2.title: Bishop and knight
s2_3_2.desc: Both kings, a bishop, a knight, six pawns.

s2_3_3.title: Two rooks
s2_3_3.desc: Both kings, two rooks, six pawns: several alignments.

s2_3_4.title: Twelve pieces
s2_3_4.desc: Both kings, a queen, a bishop, a knight, six pawns: the pieces and their relations.

s2_3_boss.title: The hanging piece
s2_3_boss.desc: After three moves you don't see, find the hanging piece and the capture square.

s2_3_hidden.title: Three announced moves
s2_3_hidden.desc: Three announced moves, then a question about the final position: “How many pieces attack f7?”

s2_boss.title: The Cyclops
s2_boss.desc: Rebuild a full position in 30 seconds.

s3_0_boss.title: The Juggler, short version
s3_0_boss.desc: A reminder of chapter 1 before getting into motion.

s3_1_1.title: An announced route
s3_1_1.desc: Follow a rook or a bishop along an announced route, then say which piece is captured.

s3_1_2.title: The destination square
s3_1_2.desc: Find the destination square after 2 to 4 moves.

s3_1_3.title: Knight jumps
s3_1_3.desc: The minimum number of knight jumps between two squares.

s3_1_4.title: Turns and captures
s3_1_4.desc: A route with changes of direction and captures.

s3_1_5.title: A long route
s3_1_5.desc: Follow a piece over 5 to 8 moves, then answer a question.

s3_1_boss.title: The unknown route
s3_1_boss.desc: Follow a piece along an unknown route: its final square, the captured pieces, the squares crossed.

s3_2_1.title: An announced move
s3_2_1.desc: Apply an announced move to a position of 4 to 6 pieces.

s3_2_2.title: Three moves
s3_2_2.desc: Apply three moves, then place each piece.

s3_2_3.title: The missing piece
s3_2_3.desc: A sequence with a capture: which piece has disappeared?

s3_2_4.title: Chain captures
s3_2_4.desc: A sequence with several pieces and successive captures.

s3_2_5.title: Assorted questions

s3_2_boss.title: Five moves, three questions

s3_3_1.title: The attacked pieces

s3_3_2.title: Defended or not

s3_3_3.title: The alignments

s3_3_4.title: Hanging

s4_1_2.title: Two replies

s4_2_3.title: Puzzle without a board

s4_3_2.title: Two variations

s4_3_3.title: Several defenses

s4_3_4.title: Plausible variations

s1_1.title: The obvious move

s1_mini.title: Flawless

s1_boss.title: The Metronome
s1_boss.desc: A series of mates whose length is never told. 12 correct lines in a row; a mistake resets the series. The thinking time gets shorter with each correct line.
